findings: The passive tensor polarizability obeys the lossless matrix optical theorem. Plane-wave force calibration is nonzero and has no net pure-electric-dipole self-force.

Mechanical torque about the particle center includes the angular momentum carried by its outgoing radiation. That self-field torque is nonzero for a polarized electric dipole even though its self-force vanishes.

The starter retains the correct full tensor response, radiation reaction and force. Its torque includes only the incident-field contribution; the physical correction is the outgoing angular-momentum flux.

For circular polarization in a principal plane, the total torque is proportional to |alpha_i-alpha_j|^2 and is nonzero for the stated anisotropic particle. Isotropic lossless cancellation is a diagnostic limit, not an all-zero hidden target.
The public support readout, torque origin, illumination, tensor response and point-dipole limit specify the apparatus without giving the missing recoil term or a numerical method.
The real orthogonal body rotation and independently radiation-dressed principal polarizabilities obey the tensor lossless optical theorem.

The plane-wave force coefficient and field-induced torque have the correct exp(-it) signs. The radiated angular momentum subtracts Im(p* cross p)/(12*pi); it is separate from radiation reaction in the polarizability.
The public apparatus fixes torque about the particle center and a held orientation. It supplies the full point-dipole response without the missing torque formula.

The independent total Maxwell-stress surface integral includes both incident/scattered interference and the pure scattered angular momentum. Calibration uses nonzero force and identifies the scalar strength, while all principal-axis torques vanish.
